zone_name: Central Petén Staple Foods and Cattle Farming Labor
notes: Shares measured from vector bar geometry of Figs 4-5 (p45). Mappings: 'local labour sales'+'migrant labor' -> agricultural_labor (very poor 87+3), 'forest incentives' -> transfers, 'wage labor' -> formal_employment, 'female labor' (xate/Ramon nut collection, domestic work) -> other_casual_labor, 'small business' -> self_employment_trade. Land is hectares exploited incl. pasture (very poor 2-2.8 rented; better-off '>45' ha and '>100' cattle left null); no lean season reported; calendar shows rains Jun-Nov while text says Jul-Dec; poor self-sufficient in maize 6 months, beans 3.

zone_name: South Petén, Northern Transversal Strip (FTN) and Izabal Agro-industry and Food Crops
notes: Shares measured from vector bar geometry of Figs 4-5 (p54); 'labour sales' (local farm + plantation labour) -> agricultural_labor, 'wages' (skilled work: construction, drivers, teachers) -> formal_employment, 'self-employment' -> self_employment_trade. Land in ha: middle/better-off use the text's averages (15-20 and 80-120 ha) rather than Table 1's 3-20 / 40-200 ranges; poor 0.5-1.5 ha rented. Rainfall given only as a ~2000 mm average; 'strong winds' and palm-oil land-use change/river pollution recorded as 'other'.

Chart values are embedded as data labels in the PDF text (chart_text) and match the bars; 'fish' (own catch, 40-60% stated) + 'wild foods' (2%) summed into wild_food_fishing_hunting; fishing labor -> other_casual_labor, poor 'female labor' (hotel domestic work, 10%) also added to other_casual_labor, fish sales -> natural_resources, small rental + tourism businesses -> self_employment_trade, 'wages' -> formal_employment. Land: table in ha; middle land from prose 20-40 manzanas x0.7 (report's own ha conversion is inconsistent, table shows 0); middle cattle from table cell '030' read as 0-30; better-off land/cattle unclear (prose says large herds and 45-450 ha). Hazard 'other' = lionfish, overfishing/fishing bans, river pollution; conflict_insecurity = drug trafficking.

zone_name: Coffee, Cardamom, Forestry and Vegetable Production
notes: Food/income shares estimated visually from Figures 4-5 (p72); very poor 100% labour is stated. Mapping: labour sales -> agricultural_labor, 'transfers' -> remittances, wage labor -> formal_employment; 'female income' guessed by group: poor -> self_employment_trade (tortilla sales, domestic work), middle -> self_employment_trade (added to small business 20%), better-off -> formal_employment (permanent jobs). Land table in ha (better-off '>3' left null). Hazards and coping table are on p74 (outside segment range); 'other' hazard = cash-crop price drops, strong winds, deforestation; coping 'other' = reduce non-essential spending.

zone_name: Western Highlands Labor, Staple Crops, Vegetables, Trade and Remittances
notes: Shares estimated visually from Figures 4-5 (p82); remittances 25-40% stated for poor and middle together (chart reads ~23% poor, ~40% middle). Land table in ha (poor 1-3 cuerdas = 0.04-0.12 ha); better-off land '>1 ha' and cattle '>5' left null. Hazard 'other' = landslides and strong winds; remittance_drop = deportations.

zone_name: Baja Verapaz and Quiché Staple Food and Agricultural Labor
notes: Land in ha as printed; better-off '>10 ha' recorded as 10 (lower bound) and very-poor household size '>=8' as 8. notes: Land in ha as printed (better-off '>13' recorded as 13, lower bound). zone_name: Industrial, Agri-business Labor, Commerce and Services of Central Area
notes: Land in ha as printed. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p111); 'informal labor' (factory, transport, domestic, security, construction and agri-business casual work) plus 'female labor' (domestic service, prepared food) mapped to other_casual_labor - part of it is agri-business labour; 'wage labor' to formal_employment, 'business' to self_employment_trade. zone_name: Eastern Subsistence Food Crops and Agricultural Labor (Coffee, Fruit and Vegetables)
notes: Land in ha as printed (better-off '>3.5' recorded as 3.5, lower bound); better-off cattle left null because the table says 0 while the text mentions cattle ranching. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p120); 'casual labor' mapped to agricultural_labor (mostly local farm labour), poor 'domestic labor' to other_casual_labor, 'business' to self_employment_trade, 'wage labor' to formal_employment. Hazards and coping table continue on p122, beyond the segment's last page.

Five groups: the two 'middle' entries are lower middle (11%) then upper middle (5%); land is given in ha (midpoints; better-off 23-430 ha, cattle '>500' set to 500). Most shares read from Figures 4-5 (p129); 'agri-produce trade' (coffee trading / plantation cash crops) mapped to self_employment_trade, firewood/timber to natural_resources; better-off livestock 20% and trade 40% are stated (chart shows livestock ~25%). Poor staple self-sufficiency given as 2-3 months in one place and ~4 months in the calendar text; lean season Apr/May to mid-Aug, calendar Apr-Jul.

zone_name: Southern Agricultural Industry Labor and Food Crops
notes: Land in ha as owned/cultivated plus rented (midpoints summed: middle 0.5-1 + 0.5 rented, better-off 1-2 + 7-10 rented). Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p140); 'labor sales' mapped to agricultural_labor, 'small business' to self_employment_trade, 'wage labor' plus middle 'female labor' (full-time service jobs) to formal_employment, poor 'female labor' (domestic service) to other_casual_labor. Irrigation is important for export plantations but most households lack it; lean season per calendar Jun-Jul (narrative: low labor demand May-Aug).

zone_name: Pacific Ocean Artisanal Fishing, Trade and Services
notes: Table defines very poor/poor/middle (prose calls them poor/middle/better-off); middle land cell '> 0.7 0.08' is garbled so left null. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p148); fish eaten (mostly in-kind payment for fishing labor for poorer groups) put under wild_food_fishing_hunting; 'local labor sales' (mainly fishing labor) -> other_casual_labor; fish sales -> natural_resources (text says ~half for poor and middle; chart shows ~40% for poor); 'female labor' -> self_employment_trade for very poor/poor (fish/craft selling) and formal_employment for middle (tourism wage labor). Other hazards: red tide, rough seas/warming water, resource over-exploitation, sugarcane expansion.
